### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-text-slot-template.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a6f3a13f2aea4275e2984709461e7f4b1201e17e`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-text-slot-template.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a6f3a13f2aea4275e2984709461e7f4b1201e17e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1721624a3871ce156e365eb2b97eed863e495323` — the merge of head `f915b87714d0d73d06248114fbefa1c8449fb08e` into base `a6f3a13f2aea4275e2984709461e7f4b1201e17e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1721624a3871ce156e365eb2b97eed863e495323 && git checkout 1721624a3871ce156e365eb2b97eed863e495323
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a6f3a13f2aea4275e2984709461e7f4b1201e17e f915b87714d0d73d06248114fbefa1c8449fb08e && git checkout -B drift-repro a6f3a13f2aea4275e2984709461e7f4b1201e17e && git merge --no-ff f915b87714d0d73d06248114fbefa1c8449fb08e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a6f3a13f2aea4275e2984709461e7f4b1201e17e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a6f3a13f2aea4275e2984709461e7f4b1201e17e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d693848a79f5730ceedfed23b5be0b84bdfd5fc9`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #19939 body and all 39 comments (stage plan `6096263424`, census `6096228459` rows R4–R6 and stage_plan S2, S1 ACCEPT `6101189699`, S1 landing `6101473453`, triage `6107801130`, S2 claim `6107940231`, S2 report `6108947793`); PR #22715 (merged `f66fdc7973`, 38 files) and its PASS record `6101076479`; PR #22832 body, its 23 files and `git diff origin/main...d693848a79` (merge-base `c4e7fa5a31`, +1185/−145, 23 files — equal to the PR file list); the head's check-runs (polled to completion); ruling D on #11182 (`5805777944`); ADR-0032 Decisions 2 and 3; ADR-0087 D2 and D3; `.changeset/pre.json`, `.gitignore`, the four `19939-*.md` changesets on `main`; `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`breakingDeclaration`), `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, the WHICH LEVEL prose in `pr-automation.yml`; PR #22747's line; objectui at the pin `20c6d351ad` (`initialRecord.ts`, `ScreenView.tsx`, `ObjectForm.tsx`, `previews/screen-spec.ts`, `flow-node-config.ts`); objectui#12101.

**Check-runs on `d693848a79`, polled every three minutes from 12:21Z until every run had a conclusion (12:49Z):** 35 runs, 35 completed — 33 `success`, 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`: `.objectui-sha` does not move in this diff; `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 `failure`. Green among them: `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1–6 and the roll-up, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1–3 and the roll-up, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · source gates` / `· consumer gates` / `· workspace` / `· debt ledger` and the roll-up, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, the four PR-claim guards. Every gate verdict is green; the verdict below rests on ② alone.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, the three positions.** `ScreenConfigSchema.defaults` goes from `z.record(z.unknown())` to `z.record(FlowValueSlotSchema)`; a field's `defaultValue` from `z.unknown()` to `FlowValueSlotSchema`: a single-brace token is refused at `FlowSchema.parse`, `registerFlow`, `objectstack validate` and the executor's parse; an envelope and every literal accepted as before. A narrowing only at these two. RIGHT (ADR-0032 D2 computed value is whole-field CEL, D3 single brace deleted; ruling D's C half; census R4, R5).
- **`recordId`.** `z.string()` becomes `z.union([z.string(), AssignmentExpressionValueSchema])` with the token judge on the string arm. A token is refused (narrowing); an envelope, refused at base by `z.string()` (`invalid_type`) and by the doors (`node-config-refused-by-contract@recordId`), is ACCEPTED at head: a new accepted value on a published authorable key, and the published JSON Schema (`anyOf: [string, object]`) and `ScreenConfig['recordId']` widen with it. The contract itself is RIGHT (census R6: "the contract gains the envelope arm"); its consequence for the declaration line is in ②.
- **The premise correction.** Verified by reading: at the merge base `recordId: z.string().optional()` (`builtin-node-config.zod.ts:899`), so an envelope object failed the parse, and `builtinValueJudged` had no carve-out for it (not a value slot, not a region, not run-resolved, no token). Assumption 1 was false for `recordId`, true for the other two. It makes nothing in the changeset's "Why" or the D3 entry false (neither claims an envelope at `recordId` went on the wire). It does make `Clause-②: no` wrong (②), and the changeset's "Still accepted, unchanged. A CEL value envelope …" imprecise at `recordId`, where the envelope is newly accepted.
- **Ledger.** `FLOW_NODE_EXPRESSION_PATHS` appends three `value` rows (`screen defaults.*`, `screen fields[].defaultValue`, `screen recordId`), every older row byte-identical and pinned; `fields[].visibleWhen` keeps its `predicate` row on the descriptor channel; the channel split is pinned (`config-expression-ledger.test.ts`). One judge (`flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals`) walks the ledger; no second judge. RIGHT.
- **`LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` + `screen`.** The S1 precedent for `map`: data in an existing export, read only inside spec; no `api-surface/**` or `export-origins/**` file moves (checked). Does not by itself flip the line. RIGHT.
- **The build doors' value arm (`flow-node-config-refusals.ts`, outside the claimed surface).** Both versions read. `atOrInsideJudgedLedgerSlot` skipped every issue at or inside a `value` slot; it now skips one only where the authored value at the slot is envelope-shaped. For every value slot S1 and passes 1–3 declared, the contract is `celValueSlotSchema` (`z.unknown()` plus the token superRefine), so the only issue a literal can draw there is a token refusal, which the `carriesInterpolationToken` carve-out on the next line already skips; the map itself (`fields: 'x'`) is shorter than the slot's segments in both versions. No verdict moves at `assignments.*`, `fields.*`, `input.*`, `inputs.*`. At `recordId` a literal the contract refuses for its type (`42`, `null`, a list) keeps being reported, as it was when `recordId` was not a slot. Without this edit the doors would have gone silent on `recordId: 42` — a widening the dev caught. RIGHT; pinned (`flow-builtin-node-config-values.test.ts`), ablation 4.
- **`insideValueSlot` and `[]`.** Base split the path on `.` and matched `*` against any segment; head uses `ledgerSlotSegments` + `startsWithLedgerSlot` (`*` any string key, `[]` any index). For a map slot a record key is always a string, so the two match identically on every pre-existing slot; only `fields[].defaultValue` (new) changes, where a malformed envelope was double-reported as `node-config-key-required-by-rule` at `fields[0].defaultValue.source`. RIGHT; ablation 5.
- **Executor.** `recordIdOf`: absent → `undefined`; otherwise `resolveValueSlot`, the S1 shape (`isExpressionEnvelopeShaped ? engine.evaluateValueEnvelope(value, variables, where, context) : interpolate`), a literal string returned as the contract's string; an envelope must evaluate to a non-blank string or the node throws, naming its source, never `String(value)`. `defaults` through `resolveValueSlotMap`, each field's `defaultValue` through `resolveValueSlot` with `fields[i].defaultValue` as its label. No `??` to the interpolator anywhere (the only `??` is the pre-existing `map ?? {}`). The map resolver now calls the single-value one per key, so the dispatch is spelled once; the S1 callers (CRUD, subflow, map, script) are behaviour-identical. A pass-through screen evaluates nothing (pinned). RIGHT; ablations 1, 2.
- **Null and absent, per position, on the served screen.** Pinned through the shipped engine (`screen-value-slots.test.ts` §3): unguarded absent fails the run at each position naming its source; guarded `null` served at `defaults.*` and `defaultValue`; `recordId` refuses `null`, a map, a list, a blank string; the template's `[object Object]` is gone. The client consequence is read at the pin: `resolveInitialRecord` keeps a `null` member; `initialScreenValues` seeds any non-`undefined` `defaultValue`; `ObjectForm` with `mode: 'edit'` and no `recordId` throws "Invalid form mode or missing record ID" on save and reads a record only when `mode !== 'create'`. RIGHT.
- **The edit/create consequence in the changeset.** The edit consequence is stated ("its `edit` form opened with no record and could not save … route around the screen with a `decision`"). The rule is stated without a mode qualifier ("Anything else, `null` included, fails the run at the screen"), so it describes the uniform rule the dev shipped. Not false; "in either mode" would make it explicit. Non-blocking.
- **The screen sentence.** `SCREEN_VALUE_SLOTS` keyed by the ledger entry, like S1's `CALLEE_INPUT_SLOTS`; `absentCaseOf` factored out of `calleeSentence` with the same truth table; reaches the two build doors and the lint hints through the one judge; the executor parse carries the base remedy alone (the S1 boundary). Six judge pins; ablation 6. RIGHT.
- **Lint.** No `packages/lint/src/*.ts` source line moves; both hints flip by asking the judge (6 pins). No lint entry owed. RIGHT.
- **Descriptor.** `screen-nodes.ts` keeps `recordId: { type: 'string' }` and `defaults` open; the engine reads a descriptor's `configSchema` for undeclared keys only ("structural only — no validation semantics", `engine.ts:189`), and `screen` is key-judged by the spec, so the descriptor's type refuses nothing. The Studio form consequence is objectui#12101's. RIGHT.
- **Sites.** CRM `crm_convert_lead_wizard` 3 `defaults` values (census R4: 3), `company` guarded, `name` and `account_id` bare with the reason in the comment; `flows.mdx` example, the value-slot list, the new paragraph; the `recordId` fixtures. Match R4–R6 counts. RIGHT.
- **Out of surface, each mechanical:** `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (+3 sites, header 705→708 matches the body, 226 schemas unchanged); `schemaless-node-config.zod.ts` (S1's `map` precedent); `value-slot-map.ts` (`resolveValueSlot`, not exported from the package entry — checked); the descriptor's three descriptions and two comments this diff made false; `builtin-node-config.mdx` regenerated (`Type Check · source gates` green); tests. RIGHT.
- **Two sibling sentences this diff makes false, which the diff does not touch and the report does not name.** (i) `packages/services/service-automation/README.md:211`: "Other value-like positions — a `filter`, `recipients`, an `http` payload, a screen's `defaults` — still read the single-brace dialect" — the README ships in the npm package (`files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]`), and `:191`'s value-slot row omits the screen positions. (ii) `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-text-slot-template.ts:171`: the `FLOW_NODE_TEXT_SLOTS` docblock lists "a screen's `recordId` / `defaults` / field `defaultValue`" among the positions keeping the single brace (S1 corrected the same docblock for its positions as a mechanical crossing). WRONG by omission; (i) is a published sentence. Both go in the patch round below.

### ② Semver level

- **Packages.** `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-automation` are the two published packages whose `src/**` moves; lint moves tests only; `@objectstack/example-crm` is `private: true`; docs are no package. No other published package moves. RIGHT.
- **Level.** `.changeset/pre.json` on `main` is `{ mode: pre, tag: next }`; `check-changeset-no-major` stands aside in pre mode; passes 1–3 and S1 graded the same two packages `major`; `Check Changeset` green on this head. `major` RIGHT. The `!` in the title, the `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM → TO table, the one-line fix, the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (already-registered flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused)` (the id exists at base and head) — all present. RIGHT.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — WRONG on the value.** The repo's definition: the value answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」; WHICH LEVEL names "a new accepted key or value" on a published payload as a widening; `clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes (narrowing)` as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read", and `no (narrowing)` as "NOT a widening, but breaking". This diff narrows (a token refused at three positions) AND widens (`recordId` accepts a CEL envelope it refused at base; its JSON Schema and inferred type gain the arm). The dev measured only the export half (`api-surface/**`, `export-origins/**` unmoved) and flagged the type widening for the seat; S1's `no (narrowing)` was right because nothing there was newly accepted (`z.unknown()` already took an envelope), and the stage plan's `no (narrowing)` rested on the premise this report itself falsified. The line should read, on both carriers (PR body line 2, `.changeset/19939-flow-screen-value-slots.md:14`): `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: a {…} token is refused at screen.defaults.*, a field's defaultValue and screen.recordId; widening: screen.recordId accepts a CEL value envelope it refused, and its published JSON Schema and inferred type gain the envelope arm)` — PR #22747's shape for a mixed change; the reader takes the arm `narrowing` from it. The level does not move (`yes` takes at least `minor`; `major` stands) and neither gate's verdict moves (`breakingDeclaration` reads the arm; the level axis is satisfied); what moves is a declaration that ships in the CHANGELOG. The changeset's "Still accepted, unchanged. A CEL value envelope …" takes the same edit at `recordId`.
- **Supersession.** S1's changeset (`19939-flow-callee-input-value-slots.md:32`) lists "a screen's `defaults`" among the positions still reading the single brace; this changeset's "supersedes that line" sentence follows S1's own precedent for pass 3. Acceptable.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (`6108947793`), each answered:
1. `flow-node-config-refusals.ts` crossing — accepted; no S1 or pass 1–3 verdict moves, the `recordId: 42` widening it prevents is real (①).
2. The other crossings (schemaless, `value-slot-map.ts`, the baseline, the descriptor text, tests) — mechanical, accepted (①).
3. `flows.mdx` two stale `subflow` lines fixed in place — same file, same defect class; accepted.
4. No regenerated `registry.ts` — verified: `.gitignore:68` is `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`, untracked at the merge base, the head and `origin/main` since #22706 (`ed1de8c2db`); the PR #22812 re-sync note does not apply. RIGHT.
5. Two merges of `main` — the merge-base diff equals the PR file list; process, no finding.
6. Attribution form — process, no finding.

Open question (`recordId` refuses a non-string evaluated id in every mode) — **A, uniform, is RIGHT.** The slot's contract and its refusal are mode-independent; `ObjectForm` reads `recordId` only when `mode !== 'create'`, so an evaluated `recordId` on a create form is dead either way and a mode branch would be a second rule for one slot kept in step with the client; the census and the grep measure zero authors writing `recordId` on a create form; loud everywhere is ADR-0032 D1's shape. The changeset's sentence carries no mode qualifier, so it already states the uniform rule.

Out-of-scope carriers, each judged:
- objectui#12101 for the Studio form (`flow-node-config.ts:857` help text `{account_id}`, `recordId` as a string input) and `previews/screen-spec.ts` — RIGHT carrier (the card says each later stage comments there; the plan says the seat extends it at ACCEPT). One precision: at the pin the preview interpolates title/description and CARRIES `defaultValue` and `defaults` as written, marking a `{…}` in `defaultValue` as "a template the run fills in" (`defaultValueTemplates`) — stale teaching, not interpolation. Nothing shipped here is false by it.
- S7 for the `validate-flow-template-paths` doubling — RIGHT, the note passes 1–3 and S1 carried.
- carrier none for the blank-`source` envelope lead at the executor parse of `recordId` — acceptable: the executor parse is the guard and the two build doors lead with `VALUE_ENVELOPE_REFUSAL` (the S1 boundary); the `ScreenRecordIdSlotSchema` docblock's "as in every value slot" over-reaches for that one case at that one door; internal, non-blocking.
- carrier none for a literal `recordId: ''` — RIGHT, unchanged from base (`z.string()` took it).
- seat post #18549's ledger for hotcrm, NOT MEASURED — RIGHT, the plan's carrier.
- none owed for `skills/**` — verified by grep at `origin/main`: no skill text names the three screen positions. RIGHT.
- Missed (①): `service-automation/README.md:211` and `:191`, and `flow-text-slot-template.ts:171` — this PR's, not a later stage's: both are the "sentence this diff made false" class S1 fixed in place.

**The patch round, one commit, re-reviewed on its head:** (1) the `Clause-②` line on both carriers, to `yes (narrowing: …; widening: …)` as spelled in ②, and the changeset's "Still accepted, unchanged" sentence at `recordId`; (2) `README.md:211` and `:191`; (3) `flow-text-slot-template.ts:171`. Everything else on this head is judged right and needs no change.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f915b87714d0d73d06248114fbefa1c8449fb08e`
Local-runs: none

Delta review of patch round 1, against the FAIL record `6109203893` at `d693848a79` and the seat order `6109208049`; the round-0 judgments on everything the delta does not touch stand as written there.

Read: the two commits since `d693848a79` — `91688dfdde` (merge of `origin/main` `a6f3a13f2a`, parents `d693848a79` + `a6f3a13f2a`) and `f915b87714` (text only, +19/−14 in 5 files) — `git diff 91688dfdde f915b87714` in full; `git diff d693848a79 91688dfdde` restricted to the 26 PR files (empty); `main`'s moved paths from `c4e7fa5a31` to `a6f3a13f2a`, and from `a6f3a13f2a` to the current `origin/main` `31b5a5f7f5` (three later commits: cli, plugin-webhooks, platform-objects), intersected with the 26 PR files (empty both times); the PR body after the `issue_patch` (line 2, line 93, the footer); the dev's report `6109593912`; the posted record `6109203893`; `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (`CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE`, `matchValueToken`, `readArmToken`, `clause2LineDescribes`, `hasInlineClause2Key`, `readClause2Line`); zod 4.6.x `handleUnionResults` and `util.aborted` and the `$ZodCheck` `continue: !def.abort` flag, in the installed package; `expression.zod.ts` `EvaluatedExpressionSchema`; `.changeset/22110-flow-text-slot-double-brace.md:24` and `19939-flow-callee-input-value-slots.md:32` on `main`; #22586 (body and four comments); the head's check-runs.

**Check-runs on `f915b87714`:** 42 runs, 42 completed — 38 `success`, 4 `skipped`, 0 `failure`, 0 pending. The four skips: `Console Pin Gate` (the pin does not move) and `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, plus `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` on the second `pr-automation` run `38143745635`, the one the body edit triggered, where both are by-design skips and whose `Check Changeset` is `success` beside the first run's. Green among the required set: `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1–6 and the roll-up, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1–3 and the roll-up, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, the four `Type Check ·` jobs and their roll-up, `Check Changeset` (both runs), `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, the four PR-claim guards. `mergeable_state` is `clean`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta is text.** `f915b87714` touches a changeset, a README, two JSDoc blocks and one comment: no Zod rule, no executor line, no test, no ledger row, no generated artifact moves. The merge commit `91688dfdde` changes none of the 26 PR files, and nothing `main` moved since the merge base — through `a6f3a13f2a` or through the three commits after it — intersects them. Every ① judgment of round 0 holds unchanged on this head. RIGHT.
- **The two extra edits, each true at `f915b87714`.** (a) `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:3198`: "interpolated" → "resolved" — the comment describes what a `ScreenSpec` carries on that route, and at this head `screen-nodes.ts` resolves `defaults` / `defaultValue` through `resolveValueSlotMap` / `resolveValueSlot`; the `{record.email}` on the next line is the measured history the comment recounts. True; comment-only, so it owes no `@objectstack/runtime` entry (`Check Changeset` green, and the level axis grades only packages whose published source moves). (b) The `ScreenRecordIdSlotSchema` docblock now says the union's own parse leads with `VALUE_ENVELOPE_REFUSAL` "except for an envelope the envelope arm parses and then refuses (a blank `source`): the union reports that arm's own sentence." Confirmed by reading zod's union: `handleUnionResults` returns an option's own result when exactly one option is non-aborted; `util.aborted` reads an issue without `continue: true` as aborting; a `.refine()` issue carries `continue: !def.abort`, so `true`. For `{ dialect: 'cel', source: '' }` the string arm aborts (`invalid_type`) and the envelope arm's only issue is the `NON_BLANK_STRING` refine on `source` (`EvaluatedExpressionSchema`), so that arm is returned as is and the union's `error` map, which fires only on `invalid_union`, never runs: the sentence is `EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED` at `recordId.source`, without the lead. For `{ dialect: 'cel' }` (`invalid_type` on `source`) and `{ dialect: 'template', … }` (`invalid_value` on the literal) both arms abort, `invalid_union` fires and the lead applies — the two shapes the spec pin covers. The narrowed docblock is exactly what holds. RIGHT.
